暴.meaning: Under a blazing <part>sun</part>, a polite garden party sips tea, until one guest flicks a drop at another. Seconds later it's a full <part>water fight</part>: buckets, hoses, cake flying, Grandma on the table with a super-soaker. Nobody saw such an <kanji>outburst</kanji> coming.
暴.on: It ends when someone rolls a <sound>bou</sound>lder into the pond and soaks everybody at once.
暴.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' shrieks the host as the <sound>ba</sound>rbecue tips into the pool and the guests run wild.

類.meaning: A <part>large</part> chef spills a sack of <part>rice</part> into a bath full of toys. Grumbling, he fishes out every grain and every <part>rubber duck</part>, ducks in one pile and grains in another, by size and colour. He means to <kanji>sort</kanji> it all before dinner.
類.on: The bath stands in a crumbling old <sound>rui</sound>n, so he works by candlelight.
類.kun: Under the grains he finds a <sound>ta</sound>co stuck to a duck with green <sound>goo</sound>: a new kind altogether.

似.meaning: A puppy copies everything its owner does. The owner hangs his scarf on the <part>coat hook</part>, so the puppy hangs its lead there too, <part>because</part> that's what he does. Day by day the puppy is <kanji>becoming</kanji> just like him, glasses and all.
似.on: They even drive the same muddy <sound>jee</sound>p, the puppy in a tiny one behind.
似.kun: When the owner scratches his k<sound>nee</sound>, the puppy scratches its knee too.

争.meaning: Two gardeners both want the last sunflower seed in the shed. One snatches a <part>boomerang</part>, the other a <part>rake</part> and a <part>crowbar</part>, and they circle each other over the tiny seed. Neither will give in. They <kanji>contend</kanji> till sunset.
争.on: In the end both slip on a bar of <sound>soa</sound>p left on the shed floor.
争.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' '<sound>Rah</sound>!' they yell, and tumble onto an old <sound>so</sound>fa, still wrestling.

呼.meaning: A lonely fisherman has no bait, so he ties a big painted <part>mouth</part> to the end of his <part>fishing rod</part> and dangles it over the lake. Each time he jiggles the line, the mouth shouts 'Dinner!' and fish come swimming. That's his way to <kanji>call</kanji> them.
呼.on: A <sound>ko</sound>ala in the tree above hears it too and drops into his boat, hungry.
呼.kun: '<sound>Yo</sound>!' he shouts to his pal, a <sound>bu</sound>ll grazing on the shore. 'Come and see!'

玄.meaning: On a dusty shelf sits a jar with a tight <part>lid</part>. Inside, something dark and smoky curls into a slow <part>twist</part>, though nothing ever touches it. Nobody remembers who put it there or what it is. It's utterly <kanji>mysterious</kanji>.
玄.on: The jar stands by the bi<sound>g</sound> <sound>en</sound>trance door, and every guest who passes it shivers.
玄.kun: At midnight a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo pecks the lid, and a black <sound>ro</sound>dent scurries out.

率.meaning: A snowman tailor sews his coats by one strict rule: for every <part>spool</part> of thread, exactly <part>ten</part> buttons made of <part>ice</part>. One button more and the coat sinks; one fewer and it flaps open. Everything depends on the <kanji>ratio</kanji>.
率.on: He counts out the buttons on <sound>Ritz</sound> crackers, one button per cracker.
率.kun: In his best <sound>hee</sound>ls, he leads a parade of <sound>ki</sound>wi birds in ice-button coats down the street.

隊.meaning: A <part>pig</part> with plastic <part>horns</part> on its helmet marches out in front, waving a <part>pennant</part>. Behind it come four hundred more pigs, all in step, all horned, all grunting the same march. It's the farm's proudest <kanji>regiment</kanji>.
隊.on: Every soldier pig wears a smart striped <sound>tie</sound> under its chin.

将.meaning: Clinging to the top of a <part>climbing pole</part> by one <part>claw</part>, a cat swings a <part>golf club</part> at the crows circling below and yells orders to the kittens. Every kitten copies her swing. She's clearly their <kanji>leader</kanji>.
将.on: Each evening the kittens put on a <sound>show</sound> in her honour, golf clubs and all.
将.kun: '<sound>Ma</sound>!' they cry, and she tosses each kitten a <sound>sa</sound>rdine: exactly one each.

弾.meaning: An archer finds his <part>bow</part> far too slow, so he invents something <part>simple</part>: he bends it backwards and flicks dried peas off the string. They whistle across the field and punch through a fence. Each pea flies like a <kanji>bullet</kanji>.
弾.on: One pea zips down the stairs into the <sound>dun</sound>geon and rings off the bars.
弾.kun: Later he props the bow on his <sound>hee</sound>l and strums its string: tonight he plays it like a harp.

犯.meaning: A tiny <part>seahorse</part> picks the lock of its tank with a bent <part>fishhook</part>, swims through the pipes and empties the aquarium's tip jar. By dawn it's back home, innocent face on. It's the perfect <kanji>crime</kanji>.
犯.on: The only clue is a sticky trail of <sound>hon</sound>ey along the pipes.
犯.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' gasps the old <sound>ca</sound>rp in the next tank, who saw it all.

伸.meaning: A shop hangs its wooden <part>monkey sign</part> from a <part>coat hook</part> by the door. Every night the painted monkey's arms grow a little longer, until they wrap round the whole street. The sign just keeps getting bigger; watch it <kanji>expand</kanji>.
伸.on: The long arms even reach a passer-by and give his <sound>shin</sound> a cheeky kick.
伸.kun: '<sound>No</sound>!' squeals the shopkeeper as the arms stretch right round the corner.

刑.meaning: A sailor has stolen from the captain's cabin. His sentence: jump the same <part>hurdle</part> on deck all afternoon, while the bosun pokes his bottom with a blunt <part>dagger</part> each time he slows. On this ship, that's how they <kanji>punish</kanji> thieves.
刑.on: And what did he steal? Not gold, but the captain's birthday <sound>ca</sound>ke.

像.meaning: In the town square a stone <part>elephant</part> stands so still that everyone uses its curled trunk as a <part>coat hook</part>. Hats, scarves and umbrellas dangle from it all winter. At midnight it sighs and shakes them off, but by day it's a <kanji>statue</kanji> again.
像.on: Round its plinth a <sound>zo</sound>diac wheel is carved, and it stands on its own sign.

挙.meaning: In a classroom, <part>eight</part> pupils all know the answer. Each <part>hand</part> shoots up so fast that a <part>sparkle</part> crackles at the fingertips. The teacher has to wear sunglasses every time they <kanji>raise</kanji> them.
挙.on: He buys the sunglasses from a little <sound>kio</sound>sk at the back of the room.
挙.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>! Me! Me!' they shout, stretching higher and higher.

創.meaning: Deep in a dark <part>warehouse</part>, a night guard slits open an ancient crate with his <part>dagger</part>. Out tumbles a tiny glowing world: seas, mountains and a first sunrise no bigger than a coin. He's watching its <kanji>genesis</kanji>.
創.on: The first mountain on the tiny world is made of <sound>soa</sound>p, foaming at the peak.
創.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' the guard sneezes, and from the spray a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo is made: his first creation.

災.meaning: A dragon learning to drive ignores every <part>speed zone</part> sign and roars through town breathing <part>fire</part> at each red light. Hedges blaze, bins melt, and the bakery roof flies off. His driving lesson is a total <kanji>disaster</kanji>.
災.on: His instructor tries to put out the flames with a jug of <sound>ci</sound>der.
災.kun: '<sound>Wah</sound>!' wails the instructor as they crash through the ba<sound>za</sound>ar, then '<sound>Wah</sound>!' again at the fountain.

更.meaning: A barber works so slowly that the <part>sun</part> sinks behind the shop while his <part>scissors</part> snip at <part>one</part> customer's single hair. Snip... snip... the streetlights flicker on. It's beginning to <kanji>grow late</kanji>.
更.on: To stay awake he licks an ice-cream <sound>co</sound>ne between snips.
更.kun: He offers the customer a <sound>sa</sound>rdine, cries '<sound>Rah</sound>!' and snips even more.

激.meaning: A polite <part>white</part> cloud has held in its <part>water drops</part> all week. The moment it's <part>set free</part>, it hurls them down in a storm, flattening tents, snapping umbrellas and flinging hats into the sea. That's one <kanji>violent</kanji> cloud.
激.on: A tiny <sound>ge</sound>cko clings to the lighthouse window through the whole storm.
激.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' laughs the cloud. 'Try and <sound>ge</sound>t dry now!'

油.meaning: A robot's knees squeak, so it drinks <part>water drops</part> from the tap. Still squeaky. It sits down to work out the <part>reason</part> and realises robots don't want water at all. What it needs is <kanji>oil</kanji>.
油.on: It squeezes a <sound>yu</sound>zu over its knees as well, just for the smell.
油.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' it sighs as the oil goes in, then charges down the street like a <sound>bu</sound>ll, yelling '<sound>Rah</sound>!'

域.meaning: A beetle builds a tiny <part>fort</part> on a heap of <part>soil</part> and scratches a circle round it with a twig. Every ant that crosses the line is chased off with a growl. That circle is his whole <kanji>range</kanji>.
域.on: An <sound>ee</sound>l and a <sound>ki</sound>wi try to sneak across the line, and both get growled at.

巻.meaning: A <part>scarecrow</part> keeps the farm's rules painted down a <part>cobra</part>'s long back. When the farmer asks to read them, the cobra rolls itself up tight, then slowly unrolls, rule by rule. It's the farm's living <kanji>scroll</kanji>.
巻.on: Rule one, near its tail: keep off the pink <sound>car</sound>nation bed.
巻.kun: At bedtime the cobra's <sound>Ma</sound> winds it back up into a tight roll.

陸.meaning: A fish is tired of water. It plants a <part>pennant</part> on a heap of <part>soil</part>, grows two wobbly <part>legs</part> and waddles up the beach to claim it while the seagulls stare. For the first time ever, a fish has reached <kanji>land</kanji>.
陸.on: Behind it lies the <sound>ree</sound>f it left, and above it a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo shouts the news.
陸.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' gasps its cousin, a <sound>ca</sound>rp, watching it climb a hill.

離.meaning: A <part>sparrow</part> gets one tail feather caught in an <part>animal trap</part>. She doesn't panic: she wiggles, pops the feather loose and flies off, leaving it behind in the jaws. Birds know just how to <kanji>detach</kanji>.
離.on: She lands on a coral <sound>ree</sound>f far out at sea, as far from traps as she can get.
離.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' she laughs, nibbling a crumb of <sound>na</sound>an, miles away from that trap.

脱.meaning: A cheeky <part>imp</part> sneaks out under the full <part>moon</part> for a midnight swim. Off come his boots, his hat and his tiny striped socks, flung into the reeds one by one. Only an owl watches him <kanji>undress</kanji>.
脱.on: A gang of frogs plays <sound>darts</sound> on the bank, using his hat as the board.
脱.kun: He leaves the rest of his clothes folded in a cosy <sound>noo</sound>k of an old tree.

島.meaning: A huge <part>bird</part> grows tired over the ocean and lands on a lonely <part>mountain</part> poking out of the waves. It nests there so long that grass grows on its back and crabs move into its feathers. Sailors now mark it on maps as an <kanji>island</kanji>.
島.on: The only thing ever seen moving is one giant <sound>toe</sound>, wiggling at the shoreline.
島.kun: A lost <sound>shee</sound>p swims ashore, bleating for its <sound>Ma</sound>.

静.meaning: Two brothers <part>contend</part> all day over the TV remote, shouting and wrestling. Then their mum paints the playroom a soft <part>blue</part>, and the moment they walk in they yawn, sit down and start whispering. Now it's always <kanji>quiet</kanji>.
静.on: She keeps the remote locked in a steel <sound>sa</sound>fe, just in case.
静.kun: They count <sound>shee</sound>p, then <sound>zu</sound>cchinis, until they both drop off.

筋.meaning: Every night under the <part>moon</part>, a panda curls a barbell made of <part>bamboo</part> with a melon tied to each end, flexing one <part>muscle</part> after another in the pond. The other pandas just eat their bamboo. He has turned himself into pure <kanji>muscle</kanji>.
筋.on: A <sound>kin</sound>gfisher dives for the fish he scares out of the pond with every grunt.
筋.kun: After training he eats <sound>su</sound>shi in the back of a <sound>jee</sound>p, every sinew aching.

益.meaning: At the school fair, a goat with stubby <part>horns</part> licks clean <part>one</part> <part>dish</part> after another, all <part>eight</part> of them. The washing-up team cheers: no scrubbing tonight. Everybody gets the <kanji>benefit</kanji>.
益.on: An <sound>ech</sound>idna rolls under the table and polishes the dishes dry with its spikes.
益.kun: '<sound>Ma</sound>, more!' bleats the goat, and the pile of clean dishes keeps on increasing.

羽.meaning: A snowman wants to fly, so he sticks chips of <part>ice</part> in neat rows down both arms, like wings. He flaps, hops and lifts one inch off the ground before they melt. Next time, he'll borrow some real <kanji>feathers</kanji>.
羽.on: He cheers himself up with a hot bowl of <sound>u</sound>don, which melts his arms a bit more.
羽.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' honks a goose, catching his falling ice in a <sound>ne</sound>t.
